title: PRD: Hosted endpoint lane-slicing, scope changes, and launch checklist for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
creator: Maya Patel
description: High-level PRD to define lane decomposition (latency-sensitive, cost-optimized, high-throughput) across the hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Clarifies scope changes requested by sales and platform teams, defines acceptance criteria for launch, and provides an explicit checklist for cutover and rollback. This ticket coordinates PM, Eng, DX, and SRE deliverables.
goals: Ship lane-aware hosted endpoint surface so customers can select latency/cost/throughput profiles via API param
Ensure uniform behavioral contracts across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank lanes
Provide operational runbooks and telemetry to meet SLA targets for each lane
Minimize customer migration friction (default behavior preserved unless lane parameter specified)
non_goals: Building new model training or evaluation datasets (outside scope of serving surface)
On-prem private deployment changes — this PRD focuses on hosted endpoints only
Deep SDK rewrites; SDK surface updates handled in separate ticket with smaller scope
lane_definitions: latency-sensitive: prioritized for single-token/prompt latency (SLO: p95 <= 120ms for short prompts). Uses minimal batching, hot-kernel scheduling, and small-context KV shortcuts
cost-optimized: prioritized for per-token cost reduction via batching, quantized variants and caching; higher tail-latency accepted (SLO: p95 <= 600ms)
high-throughput: prioritized for bulk embedding/rerank workloads with large batch windows and autoscaling throughput targets
endpoint_mapping: chat: supports all lanes; default is latency-sensitive for interactive apps. Accepts 'lane' parameter in request body header or route param
completions: default cost-optimized lane for batch generative jobs, but supports explicit lane override
embeddings: default high-throughput; supports cost-optimized lane for small-volume requests
rerank: default high-throughput; provides optional deterministic mode for evaluation workloads

success_metrics: Lane adoption: >= 10 customers using non-default lane within 30 days of GA
Latency SLOs: latency-sensitive lane p95 < 150ms for 90% of traffic over first 7 days
Cost: cost-optimized lane reduces per-token cost by >= 25% in benchmark bench-suite-124
Reliability: no more than 1 Sev2 incident attributable to lane routing in first 30 days
Rollback readiness: <30 minute median time to revert lane routing via feature flag
acceptance_criteria: API: 'lane' parameter accepted at endpoint level for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank; schema documented in API reference
Behavior: default behavior unchanged when 'lane' omitted
Compatibility: backward compatibility smoke tests pass across 5 canonical prompts per endpoint
Metrics: per-lane telemetry emitted (latency, error_rate, cost_per_token, throughput) with tags: lane, model_variant, region
Ops: SRE runbooks for lane failover and capacity fallback exist and are validated in a table-top exercise
Canary: Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for 48 hours with automated rollback on preset thresholds
Docs: Console UI shows lane selection and cost estimates; API docs and changelog updated
Security: Any new data path audited; security_review_required = true and review completed
dependencies: ENG-23102: serving-runtime kernel selection for lane-aware scheduling
ENG-23890: routing service feature-flag and fallback policies
ENG-24011: telemetry pipeline adds lane dimension and cost tagging
DES-7603: console lane selector UX and cost estimation microcopy
rollout_strategy: Phase 0 - Internal alpha: enable lanes behind org-level feature flag for Redwood internal teams
Phase 1 - Canary: 5% production traffic for non-critical orgs; monitor telemetry and user-visible regressions
Phase 2 - Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 3 days each if no rollback triggers
Phase 3 - GA: open opt-in for all customers and update default lanes for new tenants only (existing behaviour preserved)
Rollback triggers: lane-specific error_rate > 0.5% sustained over 10 minutes, latency p95 breach > 2x target, or customer-impacting regressions reported

OpenAPI schema updated and published; sample requests for each lane included
Backend: routing feature flag implemented and end-to-end smoke tests green in staging

DX: CLI/REST examples and minimal console integration validated by design
QA: cross-protocol regression suite executed (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) with pass rate >= 98%
Security: privacy/data-flow review completed and signed off by security team
SDK: REST compat tests pass; language SDK changes deferred to follow-up ticket but docs include migration note
Legal/Compliance: pricing and SLA updates reviewed and approved
Go/No-go: Exec signoff checklist completed with votes from PM, Eng, SRE, Security, and Design
testing_plan: Unit: lane selection unit tests across all endpoints
Integration: staging routing tests that exercise fallback when a lane's backend capacity is exhausted
Perf: automated bench runs comparing lane vs baseline under synthetic and sampled workloads
Chaos: limited fault injection to validate graceful degradation and fallback policies
User: pilot customers onboarded to provide qualitative feedback before GA

aggregates: p50/p95/p99 latency per lane, error_rate per lane, cost_per_token estimate per lane
business: lane adoption rate, revenue uplift for premium lanes, customer complaints tagged to lane
